1. # View Design: `mm::virt::vmem` (`Vmem`)
2. 
3. ## Abstract Resource
4. 
5. A `Vmem` is an **owned virtual address space**: a partial map from page-aligned
6. virtual addresses to backing physical frames, carrying per-page access
7. permissions and copy-on-write (CoW) state, split into a **kernel half** (shared
8. across address spaces) and a **user half** (per-process, privately owning its
9. `UserFrame`s). It is the unit the kernel loads into the MMU — its page
10. directory's physical address is the value programmed into CR3 — and the unit of
11. fork-time CoW sharing.
12. 
13. The View models the **structure** of this address space (which addresses map to
14. which frames, with which permissions and CoW marks, plus the page-directory
15. base). It deliberately does **not** model byte-level memory *contents* (see
16. *Rejected Alternatives*).
17. 
18. ---
19. 
20. ## View Struct
21. 
22. ```rust
23. verus! {
24. 
25. /// Abstract access permissions of a mapped page, as observed by callers
26. /// (e.g. through `PageTableEntry::flags().is_writable()`).
27. pub struct PagePerms {
28.     pub read: bool,
29.     pub write: bool,
30.     pub exec: bool,
31. }
32. 
33. /// Abstract state of a single user-space mapping.
34. pub struct UserPageView {
35.     /// Physical base address of the backing user frame.
36.     pub frame: nat,
37.     /// Access permissions currently in effect for the page.
38.     pub perms: PagePerms,
39.     /// Whether the page is marked copy-on-write.
40.     pub cow: bool,
41. }
42. 
43. /// Abstract state of a single kernel-space mapping.
44. pub struct KernelPageView {
45.     /// Physical base address of the backing kernel page/frame.
46.     pub frame: nat,
47.     /// Access permissions currently in effect for the page.
48.     pub perms: PagePerms,
49. }
50. 
51. /// Abstract state of an entire virtual address space.
52. pub struct VmemView {
53.     /// User half: page-aligned user vaddr -> mapping. Domain = present user pages.
54.     pub user: Map<nat, UserPageView>,
55.     /// Kernel half: page-aligned kernel vaddr -> mapping. Domain = present kernel pages.
56.     pub kernel: Map<nat, KernelPageView>,
57.     /// Physical base address of the page directory (the value loaded into CR3).
58.     pub pgdir: nat,
59. }
60. 
61. } // verus!
62. ```
63. 
64. `view()` is exposed as `pub closed spec fn view(&self) -> VmemView` on `Vmem`
65. (public so callers can reference abstract state; closed so the mapping from the
66. four internal `LinkedList`/`Rc<RefCell<…>>` fields does not leak).
67. 
68. ---
69. 
70. ## Address-partition spec helpers
71. 
72. The classification predicates (`is_user_addr`, `is_user_region`,
73. `is_physical_region`) are **pure, total, instance-independent** functions of the
74. address only — they take no `&self`. They are therefore modeled as free spec
75. functions over architectural constants, **not** as View fields.
76. 
77. ```rust
78. verus! {
79. 
80. // Architectural constants (correspond to `sys::config` memory-layout values).
81. pub spec const USER_BASE: nat;        // first user-space address
82. pub spec const USER_END: nat;         // one-past-last user-space address
83. pub spec const PHYS_MEM_SIZE: nat;    // size of valid guest physical memory
84. pub spec const PAGE_SIZE: nat;        // == arch::mem::PAGE_ALIGNMENT
85. 
86. pub open spec fn is_page_aligned(a: nat) -> bool { a % PAGE_SIZE == 0 }
87. 
88. pub open spec fn spec_is_user_addr(a: nat) -> bool {
89.     USER_BASE <= a < USER_END
90. }
91. 
92. pub open spec fn spec_is_kernel_addr(a: nat) -> bool {
93.     // Total partition over the addressable space: kernel == not user.
94.     !spec_is_user_addr(a)
95. }
96. 
97. /// `[start, start+size)` lies entirely in user space; rejects zero size and
98. /// any range whose end exceeds `USER_END` (overflow/wrap is impossible in `nat`,
99. /// so an exec range that would wrap maps to one that fails `end <= USER_END`).
100. pub open spec fn spec_is_user_region(start: nat, size: nat) -> bool {
101.     size > 0 && USER_BASE <= start && start + size <= USER_END
102. }
103. 
104. pub open spec fn spec_is_kernel_region(start: nat, size: nat) -> bool {
105.     size > 0 && start + size <= USER_BASE  // wholly below the user window
106. }
107. 
108. /// `[start, start+size)` lies entirely within valid physical memory.
109. pub open spec fn spec_is_physical_region(start: nat, size: nat) -> bool {
110.     start + size <= PHYS_MEM_SIZE
111. }
112. 
113. /// Page-aligned base of the page containing `a`, and intra-page offset.
114. pub open spec fn page_base(a: nat) -> nat { a - (a % PAGE_SIZE) }
115. pub open spec fn page_offset(a: nat) -> nat { a % PAGE_SIZE }
116. 
117. } // verus!
118. ```
119. 
120. These satisfy the partition invariant `spec_is_user_addr(a) <==>
121. !spec_is_kernel_addr(a)`, which guarantees the user/kernel key sets in a
122. `VmemView` are disjoint.
123. 
124. ---
125. 
126. ## Well-formedness Invariant
127. 
128. ```rust
129. verus! {
130. impl VmemView {
131.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
132.         // User keys are page-aligned user addresses.
133.         &&& forall|v: nat| #[trigger] self.user.contains_key(v)
134.                 ==> spec_is_user_addr(v) && is_page_aligned(v)
135.         // Kernel keys are page-aligned kernel addresses.
136.         &&& forall|v: nat| #[trigger] self.kernel.contains_key(v)
137.                 ==> spec_is_kernel_addr(v) && is_page_aligned(v)
138.         // User frames are valid, page-aligned, and CoW implies read-only.
139.         &&& forall|v: nat| #[trigger] self.user.contains_key(v) ==> {
140.                 let p = self.user[v];
141.                 &&& is_page_aligned(p.frame)
142.                 &&& spec_is_physical_region(p.frame, PAGE_SIZE)
143.                 &&& (p.cow ==> !p.perms.write)
144.             }
145.         // Kernel frames are valid and page-aligned.
146.         &&& forall|v: nat| #[trigger] self.kernel.contains_key(v) ==> {
147.                 let p = self.kernel[v];
148.                 &&& is_page_aligned(p.frame)
149.                 &&& spec_is_physical_region(p.frame, PAGE_SIZE)
150.             }
151.         // The page directory has a valid, page-aligned physical base.
152.         &&& is_page_aligned(self.pgdir)
153.         &&& spec_is_physical_region(self.pgdir, PAGE_SIZE)
154.     }
155. }
156. } // verus!
157. ```
158. 
159. `inv()` is the open, caller-visible predicate (placed on the `VmemView` and
160. mirrored by `Vmem::inv(&self) == self@.inv()`). The CoW invariant
161. `cow ==> !write` is the key abstraction-level property fork/page-fault callers
162. rely on.
163. 
164. > **No global uniqueness invariant.** Frames are intentionally *not* required to
165. > be uniquely owned: CoW sharing and shared kernel pages mean the same physical
166. > frame may back pages in several address spaces. Cross-`Vmem` ownership balance
167. > is a global/`Drop` concern, not a single-View property.
168. 
169. ---
170. 
171. ## Spec Transition Functions
172. 
173. All mutators preserve unchanged fields via `..self` (frame condition).
174. 
175. ```rust
176. verus! {
177. impl VmemView {
178.     pub open spec fn user_mapped(self, v: nat) -> bool { self.user.contains_key(v) }
179. 
180.     pub open spec fn spec_map(self, v: nat, frame: nat, perms: PagePerms) -> VmemView {
181.         VmemView { user: self.user.insert(v, UserPageView { frame, perms, cow: false }), ..self }
182.     }
183. 
184.     pub open spec fn spec_unmap(self, v: nat) -> VmemView {
185.         VmemView { user: self.user.remove(v), ..self }
186.     }
187. 
188.     pub open spec fn spec_map_kpage(self, v: nat, frame: nat, perms: PagePerms) -> VmemView {
189.         VmemView { kernel: self.kernel.insert(v, KernelPageView { frame, perms }), ..self }
190.     }
191. 
192.     pub open spec fn spec_mark_cow(self, v: nat) -> VmemView {
193.         let p = self.user[v];
194.         VmemView {
195.             user: self.user.insert(v, UserPageView { perms: PagePerms { write: false, ..p.perms },
196.                                                       cow: true, ..p }),
197.             ..self
198.         }
199.     }
200. 
201.     pub open spec fn spec_unmark_cow(self, v: nat) -> VmemView {
202.         let p = self.user[v];
203.         VmemView {
204.             user: self.user.insert(v, UserPageView { perms: PagePerms { write: true, ..p.perms },
205.                                                      cow: false, ..p }),
206.             ..self
207.         }
208.     }
209. 
210.     // `new_frame` is the freshly allocated private frame (an implementation
211.     // allocation choice; supplied existentially by the ensures clause).
212.     pub open spec fn spec_resolve_cow(self, v: nat, new_frame: nat) -> VmemView {
213.         let p = self.user[v];
214.         VmemView {
215.             user: self.user.insert(v, UserPageView { frame: new_frame,
216.                                                      perms: PagePerms { write: true, ..p.perms },
217.                                                      cow: false }),
218.             ..self
219.         }
220.     }
221. 
222.     pub open spec fn spec_uctrl(self, v: nat, perms: PagePerms) -> VmemView {
223.         let p = self.user[v];
224.         VmemView { user: self.user.insert(v, UserPageView { perms, ..p }), ..self }
225.     }
226. 
227.     pub open spec fn spec_kctrl(self, v: nat, perms: PagePerms) -> VmemView {
228.         let p = self.kernel[v];
229.         VmemView { kernel: self.kernel.insert(v, KernelPageView { perms, ..p }), ..self }
230.     }
231. 
232.     /// Every CoW user page overlapping `[start, start+size)` is privatized.
233.     pub open spec fn region_cow_resolved(self, start: nat, size: nat) -> bool {
234.         forall|v: nat| #[trigger] self.user.contains_key(v)
235.             && page_base(start) <= v < start + size
236.             ==> !self.user[v].cow
237.     }
238. }
239. } // verus!
240. ```
241. 
242. ---
243. 
244. ## Spec sketches per top-level entry point
245. 
246. (Contracts are written in a later phase; sketches show how each function maps
247. onto the View, demonstrating every field is used.)
248. 
249. - **`new`** → `Ok` ⟹ `self@.user == Map::empty()`, `self@.kernel` populated from
250.   the supplied kernel pages/tables, `self@.pgdir` a fresh valid base, `inv()`.
251. - **`clone`** → `Ok(new)` ⟹ `new@.kernel == from@.kernel`,
252.   `new@.user == Map::empty()`, `new@.pgdir != from@.pgdir`.
253. - **`load`** → `&self`; `self@` unchanged. (Activation sets CR3 = `self@.pgdir`;
254.   that CR3 effect is *global* MMU state, outside this View — see Rejected.)
255. - **`pgdir`** → `result.physical_address()@ == self@.pgdir`.
256. - **`map_kpage`** → req. `spec_is_kernel_addr(v)`; `Ok` ⟹
257.   `self@ == old@.spec_map_kpage(v, frame, perms)`; `Err` ⟹ `self@ == old@`.
258. - **`map`** → req. `spec_is_user_addr(v)` (else `BadAddress`); `Ok` ⟹
259.   `self@ == old@.spec_map(v, frame, perms)`; `Err` ⟹ `self@ == old@`
260.   (frame dropped, no mapping persists).
261. - **`is_user_page_mapped`** → `result == Ok(self@.user.contains_key(v))`
262.   (and `Ok(false)` when `v` not user). `self@ == old@`.
263. - **`is_user_addr`** → `result == spec_is_user_addr(virt_addr)`.
264. - **`is_user_region`** → `result == spec_is_user_region(start, size)`.
265. - **`is_physical_region`** → `result == spec_is_physical_region(start, size)`.
266. - **`try_find_user_pte`** → `Ok(Some(pte))` iff `self@.user.contains_key(v)`,
267.   with `pte.frame_number == self@.user[v].frame / PAGE_SIZE`,
268.   `pte.flags().is_writable() == self@.user[v].perms.write`,
269.   `pte.is_cow() == self@.user[v].cow`; `Ok(None)` otherwise. `self@ == old@`.
270. - **`for_each_user_mapping`** → invokes `f` exactly on `self@.user.dom()`
271.   (each page-aligned user `v`), short-circuiting on the first `Err`.
272.   `self@ == old@`.
273. - **`mark_user_page_cow`** → req. `self@.user.contains_key(v) &&
274.   self@.user[v].perms.write`; `Ok` ⟹ `self@ == old@.spec_mark_cow(v)`.
275. - **`unmark_user_page_cow`** → `Ok` ⟹ `self@ == old@.spec_unmark_cow(v)`
276.   (exact inverse of `spec_mark_cow` on a writable origin).
277. - **`resolve_cow_at`** → `Ok(true)` ⟹ `old@.user.contains_key(v) &&
278.   old@.user[v].cow` and `exists f. valid(f) && self@ == old@.spec_resolve_cow(v, f)`;
279.   `Ok(false)` ⟹ `(!contains_key(v) || !old@.user[v].cow)` and `self@ == old@`
280.   (hence idempotent: a second call returns `Ok(false)`).
281. - **`resolve_cow_for_region`** → `Ok` ⟹ `self@.region_cow_resolved(addr, size)`
282.   and pages outside the range / non-CoW are unchanged. `size == 0` ⟹ `self@ == old@`.
283. - **`user_vaddr_to_paddr`** → `Ok(p)` ⟹ `self@.user.contains_key(page_base(v)) &&
284.   p == self@.user[page_base(v)].frame + page_offset(v)`. `self@ == old@`.
285. - **`copy_from_user_unaligned`** → `&self`; errors keyed on
286.   `!spec_is_user_region(src, size)` / `!spec_is_kernel_region(dst, size)` /
287.   `size == 0`. `self@ == old@`.
288. - **`copy_to_user_unaligned_unchecked`** → error predicate is a pure function of
289.   `(self@, dst, src, size)` (user/kernel/physical-region + size==0), so a `Ok`
290.   dry run guarantees the matching real run passes validation.
291.   `self@ == old@` (structure unchanged; data write is content-only).
292. - **`copy_to_user_unaligned`** → all-or-nothing: same error predicate; on `Err`
293.   no observable change, `self@ == old@`; never panics.
294. - **`copy_user_to_user`** → both ranges user-mapped; errors:
295.   `size==0`/`!user_region`/page-not-mapped (`NoSuchEntry`). Neither `self@` changes.
296. - **`memset`** → req. `self@.user.contains_key(dst)`; `self@ == old@`
297.   (content-only effect).
298. - **`unmap`** → `Ok(Some(frame))` ⟹ `old@.user.contains_key(v)`,
299.   returned frame address `== old@.user[v].frame`, `self@ == old@.spec_unmap(v)`;
300.   `Ok(None)` ⟹ `!old@.user.contains_key(v)` and `self@ == old@`.
301. - **`uctrl`** → req. `self@.user.contains_key(v)`; `Ok` ⟹
302.   `self@ == old@.spec_uctrl(v, access_perms(access))`.
303. - **`kctrl`** → req. `spec_is_kernel_addr(v)`; `dry_run == true` ⟹ validates,
304.   `self@ == old@`; `dry_run == false && Ok` ⟹
305.   `self@ == old@.spec_kctrl(v, access_perms(access))`. Dry-run error predicate is
306.   a pure function of `self@`, guaranteeing a later real run passes validation.
307. 
308. (`access_perms(access: AccessPermission) -> PagePerms` is a small spec mapping
309. from the exec permission type to the abstract triple.)
310.

312. 
313. ## Design Rationale (per field — substitution test)
314. 
315. | Field | Why callers need it | Substitution test |
316. |-------|--------------------|-------------------|

339. ## Rejected Alternatives
340. 
341. 1. **Byte-level memory contents** (`Map<nat, u8>` of physical memory).
342.    *Rejected.* The in-scope verified obligations are structural/safety
343.    properties: valid address-range classification, CoW pre-resolution,
344.    ownership balance, dry-run⇒commit determinism, all-or-nothing/no-panic.
345.    Proving byte equality for the copy/`memset` paths would require a *global*
346.    physical-memory model shared across all `Vmem`s plus a faithful
347.    physical-aliasing semantics — a far larger abstraction orthogonal to every
348.    safety property the callers actually depend on. Copy/`memset` are therefore
349.    specified as content-only (structurally `self@ == old@`) with rigorous
350.    address-validation error specs. (Deferrable to a future content-aware View.)
351. 
352. 2. **A global "is this `Vmem` active / CR3 register" field.**
353.    *Rejected.* "Active" is a property of the *global* MMU (one CR3 for the whole
354.    machine), not of an individual `Vmem`. Modeling it inside `VmemView` would be
355.    a category error. `load`'s only View-level fact is `self@ == old@`; the
356.    activation effect (`CR3 := self@.pgdir`) belongs to a separate global/HAL
357.    abstraction. `clone` still captures the observable consequence (distinct
358.    `pgdir`).
359. 
360. 3. **Mirroring the four internal fields** (`pgdir`,
361.    `kernel_page_tables: LinkedList<Rc<RefCell<…>>>`, `kernel_pages`,
362.    `user_page_tables`). *Rejected.* These fail the substitution test outright —
363.    the LRU move-to-front cache in `lookup_user_page_table`, the `Rc<RefCell>`
364.    sharing of kernel tables, and list ordering are all implementation strategy.
365.    `for_each_user_mapping`'s docstring explicitly tells callers *not* to depend
366.    on iteration order. Collapsing them into two `Map`s + one `nat` keeps specs
367.    minimal and rewrite-proof.
368. 
369. 4. **Separate `writable: bool` field instead of `perms.write`.**
370.    *Considered.* `write` is the only permission bit any caller currently reads
371.    (`is_writable`). But `uctrl(access)` sets the *full* `AccessPermission`, so a
372.    bare `writable` bool would make `uctrl`'s postcondition lossy. `PagePerms`
373.    `{read, write, exec}` gives `uctrl` a complete postcondition while still
374.    exposing `write` for the CoW invariant and PTE decode. The `read`/`exec`
375.    bits are the minimal honest completion of the permission triple `uctrl`
376.    writes; if a future reviewer judges them unused, they can be pruned to just
377.    `write` without affecting any other clause.
378. 
379. 5. **Modeling per-page *ownership tokens* (refcounts) in the View.**
380.    *Rejected.* Ownership balance (no leak / no double-free) is enforced by
381.    Rust's type system (`UserFrame` by-value transfer, `Drop`) and is reflected
382.    *observably* by domain membership: `map` adds `v` to `user`, `unmap` removes
383.    it and returns the frame, `map`-on-`Err` leaves `user` unchanged (frame
384.    dropped). An explicit refcount field would duplicate what `Drop` already
385.    guarantees and would couple the View to the `Rc` strategy.
386. 
387. 6. **A combined `Map<nat, Either<UserPageView, KernelPageView>>`.**
388.    *Rejected.* The user/kernel split is a first-class, caller-visible
389.    distinction (different ownership, different mutators, `clone` shares one half
390.    and empties the other). Two typed maps make every spec read directly and let
391.    `inv()` state the partition cleanly; a tagged union would force constant
392.    case-splitting with no benefit.

272. ## Abstract Resource
273. A `Vmem` is an **owned virtual address space**: a mapping from page-aligned
274. virtual addresses to backing physical frames plus per-page access/CoW state,
275. split into a *kernel half* (shared across address spaces, mapped via kernel page
